QS: What is middleware in ASP.NET Core?

A component in the request pipeline that receives HttpContext, can act before and after the next component, or end the request.|The pipeline is a chain of RequestDelegate functions built in Program.cs with app.Use..., in registration order.|Built-in examples: exception handler, HTTPS redirection, static files, routing, CORS, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, endpoints.
Russian dolls: each layer wraps the next, in on the way in, out on the way back.
What is custom middleware, and how do you write one?

Convention-based: a class with a constructor taking RequestDelegate next and a public InvokeAsync(HttpContext ...) method, registered with app.UseMiddleware<T>().|Factory-based: implement IMiddleware, register it in DI, then UseMiddleware<T>().|Inline: app.Use(async (ctx, next) => { ...; await next(ctx); }).|Wrap it in an extension method such as app.UseCorrelationId() for a clean Program.cs.
Convention-based vs factory-based (IMiddleware) middleware, and the scoped-service pitfall?

Convention-based middleware is constructed once when the pipeline is built, so it lives for the app's lifetime.|Injecting a scoped service (DbContext) into its constructor captures one instance forever: a captive dependency, and in Development DI scope validation throws.|Fix: take scoped services as InvokeAsync parameters, or implement IMiddleware and register it as scoped or transient so DI creates it per request.
Constructor = once forever; InvokeAsync parameters = per request.
Real example: how did you implement correlation-id and audit logging middleware in IRT?

Situation: tracing a failed shipment request across [4] services meant matching timestamps by hand in CloudWatch.|Action: a correlation-id middleware at the top of every service, an HttpClient DelegatingHandler and message headers to pass the id on, and a logging scope so every log line carries it.|Result: one Logs Insights query by correlation id shows the whole journey; support triage time dropped from [about an hour to a few minutes].
One id in, same id everywhere, one query to find it.
What are the MVC filter types and their order, and how do you write a custom action filter?

Order: authorization filters, resource filters, model binding, action filters, the action, exception filters (for errors), result filters, the result.|Custom: implement IAsyncActionFilter (or ActionFilterAttribute) and register globally, per controller, or with [ServiceFilter]/[TypeFilter] for DI.|Use filters for MVC-aware concerns: validation, auditing an action's arguments, caching a result.
Auth, Resource, Action, Exception, Result: ARAER.

IOptions<T>: singleton, read once, never reloads.|IOptionsSnapshot<T>: scoped, re-read per request, supports named options, not injectable into singletons.|IOptionsMonitor<T>: singleton, always current through CurrentValue, OnChange callbacks, named options.
Options = photo, Snapshot = photo per request, Monitor = live video.
What are hosted services and BackgroundService?

IHostedService has StartAsync and StopAsync, called by the host at startup and graceful shutdown.|BackgroundService is a base class: override ExecuteAsync for a long-running loop, honouring the stoppingToken.|Register with AddHostedService<T>() (singleton); create a scope with IServiceScopeFactory for scoped services such as DbContext.
The host's own employees: start with the app, stop with the app.
What is ILogger<T> and structured logging?

ILogger<T> is the built-in logging abstraction; T sets the log category (the class's full name) used for filtering.|Structured logging uses message templates with named placeholders, so values are stored as searchable fields, not just text.|Providers (console, Serilog, CloudWatch) decide where logs go; levels and categories are filtered in configuration.
What is rate limiting, and how do you implement it in ASP.NET Core?

Rate limiting caps how many requests a client or endpoint can make in a period, returning 429 when exceeded.|ASP.NET Core 7+ has built-in middleware: AddRateLimiter with fixed window, sliding window, token bucket and concurrency limiters, partitioned per user, IP or API key.|Apply per endpoint with RequireRateLimiting or [EnableRateLimiting]; add UseRateLimiter to the pipeline.
Bouncer with a clicker: N per window, then 429.

A lightweight way to build HTTP APIs with MapGet/MapPost lambdas in Program.cs, without controllers.|Supports DI parameters, route groups (MapGroup), endpoint filters, TypedResults, OpenAPI and, in .NET 10, built-in validation.|Great for small services and high performance; organise larger ones with route groups and extension methods.
A route and a lambda: the whole controller in one line.
What is exception middleware, and IExceptionHandler with ProblemDetails in .NET 8?

UseExceptionHandler catches unhandled exceptions from later middleware and endpoints and produces an error response.|.NET 8's IExceptionHandler lets you write handlers (TryHandleAsync) that map exception types to status codes; register with AddExceptionHandler<T>() and AddProblemDetails().|Return RFC 7807/9457 ProblemDetails with a traceId; hide stack traces outside Development.
One net at the top of the pipeline, one standard error shape.
What is IHttpClientFactory, and why not new HttpClient()?

Creating and disposing HttpClient per request can exhaust sockets (TIME_WAIT); a static HttpClient ignores DNS changes.|IHttpClientFactory pools and rotates HttpMessageHandlers (2-minute default lifetime) and gives named and typed clients configured in one place.|Add resilience with AddStandardResilienceHandler and outgoing middleware with DelegatingHandlers.
Factory = a pool of phone lines, refreshed regularly.

Span<T> is a ref struct that views a contiguous block of memory (array, stackalloc, native) without copying; slicing is free.|Because it is stack-only it cannot be a field of a class, boxed, or held across await; Memory<T> is the heap-friendly version for async code.|Used for zero-allocation parsing and buffers; ReadOnlySpan<char> for strings.
A window onto memory, not a copy.
What is IAsyncEnumerable<T> and async streams?

An asynchronous sequence: produce items with async iterators (await + yield return) and consume with await foreach.|Items are processed as they arrive instead of buffering the whole list; supports cancellation with [EnumeratorCancellation].|EF Core AsAsyncEnumerable and ASP.NET Core can stream results; System.Text.Json serialises it without buffering.
A conveyor belt you can wait on.
Response caching vs output caching vs IMemoryCache vs HybridCache?

Response caching: honours HTTP Cache-Control headers so browsers and proxies (and the middleware) can reuse responses.|Output caching (.NET 7): server-side cache of whole responses with policies, vary-by and tag-based eviction.|IMemoryCache / IDistributedCache (Redis) cache data in code; HybridCache (.NET 9) combines both with stampede protection.
Headers for clients, outputs for endpoints, data for code.
How does JWT bearer authentication work in the ASP.NET Core pipeline?

UseAuthentication runs the scheme handler: JwtBearerHandler reads the Authorization: Bearer token, validates signature (keys from the authority's JWKS), issuer, audience and lifetime, and sets HttpContext.User.|UseAuthorization then evaluates the endpoint's policies; failure gives 401 (challenge) or 403 (forbid).|Configure with AddAuthentication().AddJwtBearer() and policies with AddAuthorization.
Authentication reads the badge; authorization checks the door list.
What are keyed services in .NET 8 dependency injection?

Register several implementations of one interface under different keys: AddKeyedSingleton<ISftpClient, RebexSftpClient>("rebex").|Resolve with [FromKeyedServices("rebex")] or GetRequiredKeyedService<T>(key).|Replaces hand-written factories or Func<string, T> registrations for strategy selection.

High-performance, thread-safe producer/consumer queues: Channel.CreateBounded<T> or CreateUnbounded<T>.|Writers WriteAsync, readers ReadAllAsync; bounded channels give backpressure (wait, drop oldest or drop newest when full).|Pair with BackgroundService to decouple fast producers (HTTP requests) from slow processing.
An in-process queue with a full-sign.
What is TimeProvider and why use it?

.NET 8 abstraction over the clock and timers: GetUtcNow(), CreateTimer(), GetTimestamp().|Inject TimeProvider.System in production and FakeTimeProvider in tests to control time.|Removes flaky tests and DateTime.Now coupling; works with Task.Delay and CancellationTokenSource overloads.
Inject the clock; tests own the clock.
How do you add resilience with Polly and .NET 8 resilience handlers?

Polly v8 builds ResiliencePipelines of strategies: retry, circuit breaker, timeout, rate limiter, fallback, hedging.|.NET 8 Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience adds AddStandardResilienceHandler to HttpClients with sensible defaults.|Retry only transient errors, with exponential backoff and jitter, and make calls idempotent.
Retry, break, time out, fall back.
